items.title: Herb Ellis interviewed by Monk Rowe, Scottsdale, Arizona, April 16, 2000 [interview 2 of 2]
items.q: I remember one time I didn’t think I was getting enough money so I asked Norman for a raise.

ctx.x: What was Norman Granz like to work for?

He was wonderful. Great businessman. And he had certain rules. I remember one time I didn’t think I was getting enough money so I asked Norman for a raise. And he said, “You know better than that,” he said, “I can’t give you a raise in mid-tour.” He said, “Before the next tour we’ll negotiate.”
I see. Do you mind telling me what those kind of paychecks were like in those days?

items.title: Herb Ellis interviewed by Michael Woods, Los Angeles, California, September 3, 1995 [interview 1 of 2]
items.q: when we’d travel with Oscar in Jazz at the Philharmonic in Europe, Norman had us booked at the very best hotels.

ctx.x: In the meantime tell us about what it was like to be a musician in some of the earlier years and kind of what the pay was like.

In the earlier years? Well I was with Glen Grey, you probably don’t even remember that name but that was an orchestra, and they played pretty well. And then when I went with Jimmy I made more and this is back in the ‘40s, you know, the early ‘40s. And I finally got to making, now this will seem ridiculous, $175 a week. But back at that time that was big money you know. And then I joined Oscar and my price went up some. But I’m just amazed, and when we’d travel with Oscar in Jazz at the Philharmonic in Europe,…
Describe how things are for you now.
